memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Jacob sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph to get directions to Goshen. When they arrived in the region of Goshen," — Gen 46:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Of all the sons Jacob could have sent ahead, he sends Judah.

Think about the road Judah has travelled. He is the one who first said, "Let's sell him" (Gen 37:26-27). He is the one who walked away from his family and made a mess of his own life (Gen 38). And he is the one who, in the last chapter but one, offered to become a slave in his brother's place.

Something changed in Judah, and his father has clearly seen it. Jacob trusts him now with the most important errand of the journey — going ahead to prepare the way.

That is what grace does. It does not merely forgive a person's past; it restores them to usefulness. God does not keep His people permanently on probation. Peter denied Christ three times and was restored and told to feed the sheep (Jn 21:15-17). Paul persecuted the church and became its greatest missionary.

If you have failed badly, hear this carefully. God's forgiveness is not the end of your usefulness. It is often the beginning of it.

And it is worth noting where Judah's line ends up. From this restored man came King David, and in time the Lion of the tribe of Judah Himself (Rev 5:5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God can still use you after a serious failure?
2. Who has God restored in your life that you have written off?
3. What is God asking you to do that requires you to trust His forgiveness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your forgiveness restores me to usefulness and does not leave me on the sidelines. Give me the courage to serve You even with my failures behind me. Amen.
